newsitem.title: UK: Polish gasoline demand silent despite strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Polish gasoline demand silent despite strike threat.

text.p: Poland's second largest refinery has not stepped up its gasoline purchases despite a threatened strike at the plant, a trader at the refinery said on Wednesday.
Unions at Poland's Rafineria Gdanska SA refinery said on Tuesday they will ballot the workforce on calling a strike, in protest over delays in giving employees shares in the enterprise.
The vote should be completed by the end of January and a decision to strike could be made then.
"We don't see any impact of this development at the moment on our day-to-day trading activities," the trader said.
"There is no link between the threatened strike and Polish buying at the moment," he said.

The trader said the refinery is operating at about 60,000 barrels per day, and that it is selling its own products and not importing at the moment, which should continue until at least early February.
"For us it is a distant possibility and we don't take it into consideration," he said. "If the strike is here, then we can talk about possible implications."
The refinery already had purchased 20,000 tonnes of 95 unleaded gasoline from Norway in January, he said.

The refinery has been transformed into a state treasury controlled joint stock company as a prelude to its privatisation, and by law, employees should get up to 15 percent of shares in such companies for free.
The refinery processed 2.86 million tonnes of crude oil in 1995.
